title: Monterey Cypress: Old Monterey Cypresses You Can Visit
meta_description: In the wild it grows on two Californian headlands and nowhere else. Four Monterey cypresses mapped in Trieste, Lucca, Florence and Lisbon.
intro: In the wild this tree grows on two headlands near Monterey in California and nowhere else on earth, together covering less than a square kilometre. Give it a mild wet winter anywhere and it grows fast and enormous, which is how it reached Italian and Portuguese gardens within a few decades of being described. Trieste's stands at Miramare, put in after 1856 when Archduke Maximilian laid out a park around his castle on the sea, and is about 170 years old. Lucca's grows on the San Regolo bastion, part of the ring of Renaissance walls the city turned into a promenade. Florence has one in the Giardino Simone Weil and Lisbon one in the Parque do Caramao da Ajuda, roughly 95 years old. Four trees in four cities, all of them exiles from a coastline you could walk in an afternoon.
